key_insight: Drilled-to-bossed geometry improved AA2024-T351 friction-weld strength, while an ensemble residual network predicted ultimate tensile strength with R² ≈ 0.81.
engineering_relevance: Geometry-assisted direct drive friction welding offers a promising route to strong aluminium joints for lightweight aerospace and automotive structures.
method: Used an L18 orthogonal experimental design on a customized engine lathe.
Varied friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, interface geometry, and friction time.
Evaluated tensile and torsional strength and compared three deep learning architectures for tensile-strength prediction.
evidence_signal: The reported optimum—30 MPa friction pressure, 70 MPa forging pressure, 2200 rpm, drilled-to-bossed geometry, and 4 min friction time—achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength.
watch_item: The L18 experimental design provides limited condition coverage; predictive generalization and weld repeatability require independent validation.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
